clue.text: Items on quite strange TV show

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of these three words are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone notices peculiar items on a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters of ITEMS ON QUITE rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Question Time is a long-running BBC political debate programme, so it is a television show.

clue.text: Last drop of moonshine in fairly new still

indicators.note: in tells us the final letter of moonshine is placed within the word for fairly

parts.note: fairly means quite, as in quite good

indicators.note: the last drop of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its final letter is E

explanation.surface: A drinker tastes the dregs of illicit spirit from a nearly new distilling apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like a noun for distilling, but it is the verb to calm. E goes inside QUITE to make QUIETE, then N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To still something is to make it calm or silent, which is what quieten means as a verb.

clue.text: Cunning female pockets credit card when standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
pockets means the woman's name holds the card name inside it

parts.note: Eve is the first woman, a stock name for a female
Visa is a well-known brand of credit card

explanation.surface: A crafty woman slips a credit card into her pocket while getting to her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, is a stock crossword name for any female.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasive person dodges questions and avoids being pinned down, a sly or cunning trait.

clue.text: Show's intro gets me mostly hot 'n' bothered

indicators.note: bothered means flustered or disturbed, so the letters are shaken into a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of the word hot is used

parts.note: 'n' is a casual spelling of and, giving just N

explanation.surface: A performer feels flustered and overheated before a show begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims HOT to HO; GETS ME plus HO plus N gives nine letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme song plays at the opening of a television programme, introducing each episode.

clue.text: Circulation of gold coin

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A collector asks how widely a golden coin has been in circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: A threepenny bit was an old British coin, so 'bit' can stand for a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a path that goes round and round, a kind of circulation around a central body.

clue.text: Work to insulate home with fine wrapping material

indicators.note: to insulate something is to surround it, so the work word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: toil means hard work
in means at home
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Advice on insulating a house with a fine wrapping material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insulate' fits the home-improvement picture, but here it only means wrap around.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal sheet used for wrapping food, so it serves as a wrapping material.

clue.text: Blimey, Gila has essentially produced something that's painful!

parts.note: My! is an exclamation of surprise, like Blimey!

indicators.note: produced means made or put together anew, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the setter's own pseudonym, used as written

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter of the word has

explanation.surface: The setter exclaims at having created a painful puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Gila is the setter's own name, so the anagram fodder is the setter signing the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Myalgia is the medical term for muscle pain, a painful condition.

clue.text: Six leaders from councils exert pressure on local deputy

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
a local is someone living in the area, a resident

explanation.surface: Six council heads lean on a local deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: VI, then the first letters C and E, then P and RESIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice president is second in command, standing in for the president as a deputy.

clue.text: Surrounded by restless teething child endlessly, I get very angry

indicators.note: the letter I is surrounded by the jumbled letters around it
restless means unable to keep still, so the letters move about
endlessly means the last letter of child is dropped

explanation.surface: A parent is driven to fury by a fretful teething child.
explanation.walkthrough: CHILD loses its end to give CHIL; TEETHING plus CHIL rearranged makes HITTHECELING, with I inserted to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the ceiling is an idiom for flying into a rage, becoming extremely angry.

clue.text: One small child adopts a zoologist's last parrot

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the little one takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a mite is a small child

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word zoologist, ignoring the possessive

parts.note: the possessive belongs to the word zoologist, whose final letter is T

explanation.surface: A child takes in a parrot once owned by a zoologist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' looks like the bird adopted, but it is a verb meaning to copy. A and T go inside MITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot someone is to repeat their words mechanically, i.e. to copy or mimic them.

clue.text: Asian girl visiting African country, avoiding the easternmost part

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so the girl goes inside the country
in an across answer east is the right-hand end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: An Asian woman travels to an African country but keeps away from its eastern region.
explanation.walkthrough: Benin is a West African country; in an across answer its easternmost letter is the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bengali is a person from Bengal, a region of South Asia, so the word names an Asian.

clue.text: Twist of lemon finally placed in extremely elegant drink

indicators.note: placed in means the lemon's letter is put inside the other letters
extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters of elegant
finally points to the last letter of lemon

parts.note: its last letter is N
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A bartender adds a twist of lemon to a very elegant drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like the garnish of lemon, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine things is to twist or wind them together.

clue.text: Meditation requires but little time

parts.note: though can mean but, as in 'it rained, though not for long'
T is the abbreviation for time, a little piece of it

explanation.surface: A remark that meditation takes only a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is the act of thinking deeply, and meditation is serious, contemplative reflection.

clue.text: Extent of displeasure right at the start

indicators.note: at the start means the letter for right is shifted to the front

parts.note: anger is strong displeasure

explanation.surface: Someone measures how displeased another was from the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: ANGER ends in R; moving that R to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The range of something is its scope or reach, i.e. its extent.

clue.text: Tesla coil failing to move up and down

indicators.note: failing suggests the device breaking down, so its letters fall into disorder

explanation.surface: A malfunctioning Tesla coil cannot shift up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tesla coil is an electrical transformer; its nine letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to swing back and forth, so vibrating up and down is a form of it.

clue.text: Bespoke gear is oddly removed for clients

parts.note: bespoke means custom-made

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are taken out, leaving the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: its even letters are E, R and S

explanation.surface: A tailor's made-to-measure clothing for customers with odd bits taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Customers are the people who buy from a business, i.e. its clients.

clue.text: Archer and others succeeded after initially seeing terrible ratings

indicators.note: after means the letter for succeeded is placed behind the rest
initially points to the first letter of seeing

parts.note: its first letter is S

indicators.note: terrible means awful, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An archer and teammates succeed after seeing their poor ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archer' looks like a person, but it is Sagittarius, the archer of the zodiac. RATINGS rearranges to TARSIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittarius, the Archer, is one of the twelve zodiac signs, and the others are the rest of them.

clue.text: Island hostile to another island miles away

parts.note: anti means opposed or hostile to

indicators.note: away means the letter for miles is taken out

parts.note: Guam is a Pacific island

explanation.surface: One island is hostile to a far-off neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: GUAM loses M to leave GUA.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: More strong beer leads to excessive retching

parts.note: stout is a dark strong beer

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Stronger beer brings on heavy retching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More strong beer' reads as one phrase, but 'More strong' is the definition and 'beer' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout can mean sturdy or robust, so stouter is a comparative meaning sturdier or stronger.

clue.text: Cocaine, grass and ecstasy put in a container

parts.note: C is slang abbreviation for cocaine
to grass is to inform on someone, and to rat means the same
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs are packed into a box for smuggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like the drug, but it is British slang for informing, so it gives RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a wooden box for transporting goods, a kind of container.

clue.text: Tea includes some butter and bread

indicators.note: includes means the tea word holds the butter word within it

parts.note: chai is a word for tea
a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: A tea service that comes with butter and bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened bread of South Asia.

clue.text: Like devoted fans of Sting in a circle

indicators.note: in means the sting word sits inside the other letters

parts.note: a ring is a circle
to do someone is to swindle them, and a sting is a swindle

explanation.surface: Fans of the singer Sting gather round in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' looks like the singer, but it is a con, giving DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted fans adore their idol, so the adjective describes how they behave.

clue.text: City detective pursued by arsonists occasionally

indicators.note: pursued by means the detective comes first, followed by the other letters
occasionally means taking only some letters, here every other one

parts.note: its alternate letters are R, O, I and T

explanation.surface: A city detective chases arsonists from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a major US city in Michigan, famed for car manufacturing.

clue.text: Beneficiary follows tip from two of those people

indicators.note: follows means the beneficiary word comes after the tip
the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is T
an heir is someone who benefits from a will

explanation.surface: An heir inherits from two people.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive pronoun meaning belonging to them, i.e. of those people.

clue.text: List of top US students reportedly having repeated successes

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard spoken, the sound of a phrase

parts.note: an honor roll is a list of high-achieving students in American schools

explanation.surface: A list of top American students is said to keep on winning.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly with the H dropped, 'honor roll' sounds much like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on a roll is an idiom for enjoying a run of successes one after another.

clue.text: Close match for clothing you may go out in

definitions.text: clothing you may go out in

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A close-fitting match of clothing for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' suggests a party, but here it means fall asleep, as a light goes out. A cup tie is a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, worn in bed when you go out like a light.

clue.text: No current story brought about much joy

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the joined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A tale with no current relevance still brings great joy.
explanation.walkthrough: NO, I and TALE join as NOITALE, which read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a state of great happiness or exhilaration.

clue.text: Fancy ride-sharing apps ultimately making a bob or two?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of apps

parts.note: its last letter is S

explanation.surface: Swanky ride-sharing apps that end up earning a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a bob or two' reads as earning money (a bob was a shilling), but a bob is also a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairdressing includes cutting a bob, a short haircut, so cutting bobs is the trade.
